texto:
A community garden is a piece of land where people from a neighborhood can grow plants together. These gardens are becoming more popular in cities where many people live in apartments and do not have their own space for gardening. In these shared spaces, people plant vegetables like tomatoes and carrots, herbs like basil and mint, and sometimes beautiful flowers.

The benefits of a community garden are numerous. First, it provides fresh and healthy food for the families who participate. People learn how to grow plants and understand where their food comes from. Also, it is a great social activity. Neighbours who didn't know each other before now spend time together, share tips, and build a stronger community. It's a place where people of all ages, from young children to older adults, can work and learn together. This makes the neighborhood a friendlier place to live.

preguntas.pregunta: According to the text, what is one of the main activities in a community garden?
preguntas.explicacion: La respuesta correcta es B porque el texto menciona explícitamente que en los jardines comunitarios 'people plant vegetables like tomatoes and carrots, herbs like basil and mint'. The text clearly states this as a central activity. Las otras opciones son incorrectas. El texto no dice que vendan frutas (A), ni que construyan apartamentos (C), ni que haya clases de cocina (D) o que se estudie historia (E). The text focuses on the activity of growing plants.

preguntas.pregunta: It can be inferred from the text that community gardens...

opciones.C: can improve social relationships in a neighborhood.
opciones.D: exist only in small villages, not cities.

preguntas.explicacion: La respuesta correcta es C. Aunque el texto no usa las palabras exactas 'improve social relationships', podemos inferirlo de frases como 'it is a great social activity' y 'Neighbours... spend time together, share tips, and build a stronger community'. This implies that relationships get better. Las otras opciones son incorrectas: el texto no menciona el costo (A), dice que la gente 'learn how to grow plants', lo que sugiere que no son profesionales (B), afirma que los jardines están 'in cities' (D), y describe que crean una comunidad más fuerte, no que causen problemas (E).
